conviction_note: A mild long lean, p_up 55 on an abs move of 9.0 (implied 8.06, name median 8.14, scaled up for a likely guidance update and the hunters' record of understating moves). It rests on four things: a UBS read of positive Q3 toy POS and double-digit Wizards growth against a +5.1% Wizards consensus, Hasbro beating EPS four quarters running, a guide that passed H1 upside through while holding H2 Wizards and leaving holiday 'protection', and a possible IEEPA refund. Against it: the stock is up 13% in 20 days, and the Consumer Products consensus (+8.2%) sits above the company's own low-single-digit Q3 guide. The findings sum to +0.9, close to the scaled number, but on this name the reaction turns on the full-year guide. That guide split a raise at +8.8% from a hold at -8.8% in 2026, and no document settles which way it goes this time.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus adj EPS $1.86-1.88 and revenue $1.47-1.48bn; two sources agree. Zacks/Yahoo 2026-10-15: EPS $1.86, revenue $1.47bn, segments CP $862.3m (+8.2%), WotC $601.3m (+5.1%), CP op profit $140.7m, WotC op profit $245.7m (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stay-ahead-game-hasbro-q3-121520655.html). Investing.com 2026-10-19: EPS $1.86, revenue $1.48bn (https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/hasbro-earnings-ahead-as-gaming-division-powers-expected-beat-93CH-2743854). Earnings Whispers $1.88 / $1.49bn. Company guide: FY2026 revenue +5-7% cc ($4.94-5.03bn), adj op margin 25-26%, adj EBITDA $1.45-1.50bn (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046080/000004608026000044/exhibit991q22026.htm). On the Q2 call: Q3 Magic up mid single digits, Q3 CP up low single digits, Q4 Magic down low single digits (https://www.webull.com/news/15265615122539520). Q3 2025 base: revenue $1,387.5m, adj EPS $1.68.
positioning_check: Short interest about 5.2% of float with 2.5 days to cover (Equibles, August 2026, https://equibles.com/stocks/has/shortinterest), and 5.8% of float and rising (Benzinga, 2026-09-25, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/HAS/sentiment). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. I could not reach a fresh Nasdaq settlement (API 503). The baseline has no skew (skew_25d_vol_points null). Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.49 (call-heavy) on 3,498 total OI, and the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. Event-implied move 8.06%. The tape is +13.06% over 20 days and +4.69% over 5 days, 6.4% under the 52-week high. Citi raised its target to $117 from $107 on 2026-10-13. Consensus target is $110.64 (MarketBeat, 2026-10-14).

findings.finding: The sell-side expects more from Consumer Products than the company guided. Zacks has Q3 CP revenue at $862.3m (+8.2% y/y) and CP operating profit at $140.7m (vs $80.1m), but on the Q2 call management guided Q3 CP up low single digits (about $815-830m off a $797m base) plus part of the ~$25m of cyber-lost Q2 revenue it expects to recoup across H2. A print at the company's own guide is therefore roughly a $20-40m CP revenue miss against the published segment consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 CP fell 7% on later holiday shelf resets, and the stock still rose +3.7% on Magic and a raised guide. Q2 2026 CP grew +5% despite the cyber hit, with an +8.8% reaction. CP has not been the line this stock trades on; Wizards and the guide have.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline consensus ($1.47bn) is what the terminals carry. The gap between the segment consensus and the company's Q3 CP guidance only shows if the call transcript is set beside the Zacks segment table. Had the market priced it, headline revenue estimates would sit near $1.44-1.46bn, the company-implied sum, rather than $1.47-1.49bn.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 call transcript is a separate document (https://www.webull.com/news/15265615122539520). The counterweight is that Hasbro has beaten EPS four straight quarters by an average 23.6% and builds 'protection' into its guide, so the gap is sized small.

findings.finding: UBS (Arpine Kocharyan) cited 'broadly positive POS for the quarter' in toys and expects 'likely double digit % Wizard segment growth', against a Wizards consensus of $601m (+5.1%) and the company's Q3 Magic guide of +MSD. The industry backdrop agrees: Circana US toy dollar sales rose 17% in H1 2026, led by trading cards, collectibles and adult buyers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wizards beats drove the up-moves: Q2 2026 Magic +32% for +8.8%, Q1 2026 Magic +36% (but the guide was held and the stock fell 8.8%), Q3 2025 Magic +55% for +3.7%, and February 2026 +7.5%. Six of the last eight prints rose.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is up 13% in 20 days and Citi raised its target on 10-13. But consensus Wizards growth is still +5.1%, not double digits. If the market fully believed UBS, the published Wizards estimate would have moved toward $630m and the headline EPS estimate would not have drifted down 0.5-0.9% over 30-60 days.
findings.independence: Circana H1 2026 data (Retail Dive, 2026-08-20, https://www.retaildive.com/news/us-toy-industry-best-first-half-performance-six-years/828162/) is an industry proxy, not Hasbro's own number.

findings.finding: The full-year guide looks conservative in a way that leaves room to raise. The July raise ($4.94-5.03bn revenue, +5-7% cc) passed only H1 upside through and held back-half Wizards guidance unchanged, and the CEO said the guide carries holiday 'protection'. H1 revenue was $2,140m (+14.6%), so the guide implies H2 of about $2.80-2.89bn against $2.84bn last year (-1% to +2%). A Q3 at the $1.47bn consensus would leave Q4 implied down 2-8% y/y, more than the stated Q4 Magic decline (down LSD, $40m set shift into Q1 2027) explains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-21: beat and raise, +8.81%. 2026-05-20: beat (+13% revenue) with guide only reiterated, -8.83%. 2025-10-23: raise, +3.7%. The guide decides the sign on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic (H2 implied flat while Q3 consensus is +6%) is not in any preview I found. Previews only note that Q4 Wizards was guided down. If a raise were fully expected, the stock would already sit at or above its 52-week high, not 6.4% under it.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K guidance table is a separate primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046080/000004608026000044/exhibit991q22026.htm). The May hold shows the downside is real when Hasbro keeps protection, so the range is wide.

findings.finding: Hasbro's 10-Q says it made its first CBP CAPE application in Q3 2026 for a majority of the IEEPA tariffs it paid, and that the amounts 'could impact our results in 2026'. CBP had certified about $122bn of refunds to Treasury by mid-September, with payment generally 60-90 days after acceptance. 2025 tariff costs recognised in cost of sales were $44.9m, so a receivable or gain of a few tens of millions could appear in Q3 or flow into the Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Hasbro history. In the stage E record, tariff-refund names split up or down by guidance direction, not by the refund itself.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is undisclosed and Hasbro would likely exclude it from adjusted EPS. Nothing in the consensus or the previews models it. Had it been priced, the FY EPS estimates would have stepped up after the July 10-Q.
findings.independence: C.H. Robinson advisory on CBP refund progress, 2026-09-17 (https://www.chrobinson.com/en-au/resources/insights-and-advisories/client-advisories/2026q3/09-17-26-cbp-cape-phase-3-ieepa-refunds/). 2025 tariff cost of $44.9m from the FY2025 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/46080/000004608026000011/has-20251228.htm).

findings.finding: The cyber incident cost about $25m of Q2 revenue (against an earlier $40-60m assumption) and $10.8m of expense. Operations were fully restored ahead of schedule, and management expects the lost revenue to be recouped in the back half. No insurance recovery had been recognised yet, and one could land in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 incident print was +6.59% (2026-04-23) and the delayed Q1 full release -8.83% (2026-05-20). The latter was a guidance story, not a cyber story.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The recoup is inside the raised guide, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: 10-Q Note 2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046080/000004608026000050/has-20260628.htm) is the same company and the same facts.

findings.finding: Positioning raises the bar. The stock ran +13.1% over 20 days and +4.7% over 5 days into the print, sits 6.4% under its 52-week high, and has a call-heavy open-interest ratio of 0.49, while the EPS consensus drifted down 0.5-0.9% over 30-60 days. Short interest of about 5-6% of float and 2.5 days to cover is not a squeeze setup.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No run-up-conditioned history for this name. Six of the last eight prints rose, the largest +14.6% (2025-04-24).
findings.why_not_priced: This is what the price already says. It is filed because the run-up means part of the beat is in the stock, so a merely in-line guide carries downside. A market not leaning long would show a flat 20-day tape and no target raises.
findings.independence: Citi target raised to $117 on 2026-10-13 (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9121946/has-maintains-rating-by-citigroup-price-target-raised-to-117). Estimate drift from Investing.com, 2026-10-19.

findings.finding: Magic set flow in Q3 2026: Marvel Super Heroes, which management said set day-one and month-one records and passed LOTR as the #2 Universes Beyond set, trailed into Q3. The Hobbit (Standard-legal, launched mid-August) was planned smaller by Wizards, but its collector booster box traded at $680-891 on StockX against roughly $456 MSRP (12 x $37.99). Reality Fracture released 2 October and likely shipped to distributors before the 27 September quarter-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Magic surprises led the up-moves: Q2 2026 Magic +32% for +8.8%, and Q3 2025 Magic +55% for +3.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company's Q3 Magic guide (+MSD) already includes the release slate, so this is mostly inside the guide. What is not in the guide is sell-through quality: secondary prices well above MSRP argue against a distributor overstock read. If the market feared one, Wizards consensus would sit below the +MSD guide; it sits at +5.1%.
findings.independence: ICv2 2026-07-21 on Marvel Super Heroes records and Hobbit expectations (https://icv2.com/articles/news/view/62920/magic-the-gathering-marvel-super-heroes-passes-lord-rings). Release calendar (https://mtgrocks.com/hasbro-reveals-full-mtg-2026-calendar/). This shares the Magic line with the UBS finding but rests on a different source.

findings.finding: Licensed digital gaming is the soft line. Consensus has Digital & Licensed Gaming at $125.2m (-3.8% y/y). Monopoly GO contributed $44m in Q2 2026, flat y/y (Q1 $41m). Sensor Tower shows US store in-app purchases falling while webstore revenue grows: June 2026 US total $143m, $52.6m of it via the webstore.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Monopoly GO has not driven a print since 2024. Its contribution has been stable at $41-44m a quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus already models a decline, so this is priced. It is filed for completeness.
findings.independence: Sensor Tower via mobilegamer.biz data digest (https://mobilegamer.biz/data-digest-monopoly-gos-booming-webstore-pokemon-go-spikes-love-and-deepspace-revenue-crashes-more/).

findings.finding: John Hight, President of Wizards of the Coast, left that role on 2026-09-01 to become an advisor through September 2027 under a 27 July 8-K. No successor has been found announced, so the call may address leadership of the segment that drives the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for leadership changes at this name in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July with no price reaction attributed. It is small and filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Routine insider selling into the summer: the CFO sold 11,000 shares at $95.44 on 2026-07-28 and a director sold 1,975 at $92.84 on 2026-08-07. MarketBeat counts $4.74m sold by insiders last quarter. EDGAR shows Form 144/4 filings through 2026-09-03.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4s, small relative to holdings, and probably priced. Filed so the panel can weigh it.

outside_window.finding: Star Trek Universes Beyond set releases 2026-11-20 and the first 2027 set slips to early February, moving about $40m from Q4 into Q1 2027. That is Q4 and Q1 revenue, already in the guide, and it resolves in later prints.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly positive (beat history, positive POS read, a guide with room to raise), and so does the +13% 20-day run-up, so the long is partly priced. The baseline has no skew number, and the call-heavy open interest says the market leans the same way. That is why p_up is held at 55 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): IEEPA refund cut from +0.5 to +0.2; no stated path to the guide and Hasbro likely adjusts it out.

Lesson 6 (inside the guide): cyber recoup cut from +0.2 to +0.1, because it is inside the raised FY guide. The CP-consensus-above-guide finding eased from -0.7 to -0.6, because the segment consensus is thin and Hasbro builds protection into its guide.
Lesson 5 (proxy): insider selling eased from -0.2 to -0.1 as a weak proxy.

Lesson 1/2 (the guide decides the sign): the guidance finding is left at +0.8 with a wide -4/+5 range, and p_up is held at 55 rather than raised. The bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates, so nothing is capped. Short interest was checked: not crowded.
